title: feat: sweep briefs come from the contract; the meter holds
headline: A sweep's briefs are written from its cleared contract, each reviewer's report is checked for shape, and the findings are counted from the reports. The call cap and token ceiling now stop a reviewer in time, the cache trip counts only expired cache, and install keeps files it used to lose.
alignment: v1.37.0 is step T6 of the v2.0 plan, one checked hand-back shape for every sweep report, with the carry-overs of builds 10 and 10-fix closed in the same release.

items.text: A cleared sweep contract writes each role's brief beside it: the rules block by line range, the sweep, cap and ceiling lines, the role's diff, a scratch folder of its own and the report shape.
A reviewer's hand-back is checked once for its report shape (a role line, one five-field line per finding or No findings, and what it did not check); the second try goes through.
A sweep's outcome counts the findings from the reviewers' reports, writes a ledger beside the contract, and refuses a typed count that differs.
The release check can read a verify's result file, and passes only when one number it recorded was run again and matched.
The call-cap hook stops a reviewer while the refused call and the report still fit under its call cap and token ceiling; a reviewer the hook stopped late is named so, not as unhooked.
The cache re-write trip counts only a call that read back under half of the context before it; a large batch of new results is no re-write.
A kit script followed by another command (`&& ls`, `; git status`, `; Get-ChildItem`) is no longer held as a write to a protected file; only what runs before a program can stand in for it.
install user drops the guard record of a project folder that no longer exists, so the guard reads only the projects that exist.
Status and session start name a newer release on GitHub, and a file kept from an unreleased build with the step that clears it; the install user fix line quotes the kit folder.
Install keeps a memory file the owner's MEMORY.md still links, keeps a file the kit renamed by case alone, and never removes a file outside its folder.
The release check lists the remote's tags only at a GitHub https address and from outside the kit folder, so no program the kit folder's git config names can run.

verification: Each fix has a test that fails on 1.36.1 and passes here.
Replayed on a real 1.36.0 reviewer's call sizes, the hook stops it where the refused call and the report land under its ceiling.
Read against the 1.36.0 and 1.36.1 reviewer transcripts, the new re-write count finds no expired cache in 13 roles.

decisions.decision: The rules block is read by line range, not moved to a file of its own
decisions.why: Moving it would make every kit project move its filled block by hand; the brief's line range gives the same smaller read with no change to any project.

decisions.decision: The release check lists tags, it does not fetch
decisions.why: A fetch inside the kit folder ran a program its git config named (the push security review); a listing of a GitHub https address reads no repo config and writes nothing.

upgrading: Run `install user` first, then `install project` in each project. A sweep cleared on 1.37.0 writes its briefs beside its contract: pass each as written.
limits: The report shape and the ledger hold only where the canary runs (a project with a confirmation phrase); a sweep in the kit source counts findings by hand as before.

tests.flips: declared tests on v1.36.1 and on this branch; the PR run gives the final count
